newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts Northumbrian Water ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts Northumbrian Water ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Thursday it had lowered Northumbrian Water Group Plc's (NWG) short-term rating to A1 from A1 plus and long-term rating to A plus from AA minus.

In addition IBCA said it assigned a new short-term rating of A1 plus and a long-term rating of AA minus to Northumbrian Water Limited Plc (NWL), following the completion of a reorganisation programme at Northumbrian Water Group.
NWG is the parent of NWL, the utility appointed for water and sewerage operations in the North East of England.

"The rating movement for NWG incorporates the exposure to the financial profile of the ultimate parent, Lyonnaise des Eaux S.A. of France (LdE), following NWG's acquisition in November 1995," IBCA said in a statement.

"For LdE, the second largest water utility in France, the 820 million stg purchase of NWG represented the group's largest ever acquisition, and built on the financial year 1989 purchase of two small water supply companies, North East Water plc (NEW) and Essex & Suffolk Water plc (ESW)," the rating agency said.

"Reorganisation of the new NWG companies, which took effect on October 1, 1996, included the incorporation of pre-existing LdE subsidiaries NEW and ESW into the new entity, and the restructuring of NWG's non-regulated activities," IBCA said.

Following the reorganisation, the new NWG assumed the obligations of the 100 million stg bond issued by the pre-acquisition NWG during financial year 1993. In addition, following a 100 million stg special dividend on acquisition, it issued a further 200 million stg Eurobond in June 1996 to help refinance the acquisition burden, the agency said.

"In common with all water and sewerage companies in England & Wales, NWG's utility subsidiaries, which generated all the group's operating profits in financial year 1995, remain subject to the conditions of its appointment, including a variety of regulatory conditions policed by Ofwat, the industry regulator."
IBCA said these comprise among others, revenue caps, service targets and de facto regulatory supervision of dividend policies.

"This latter implies a degree of comfort against excessive upstreaming of dividends for the wider needs of the LdE group, as does the historical dividend policy operated by LdE with respect to its existing English water investments," IBCA said.
"More specifically, the ring-fencing measures also support a one-notch differential between parent NWG, which maintains non-regulated operations, and the utility subsidiary NWL."
